items.title: Provider snapshot replacement identity is undefined
items.statement: The unit prohibits run_id-only storage but never defines the replacement key, its tenant and account namespace, actor identifier, lifecycle, collision behavior, or migration. Concurrent non-run actors can therefore overwrite or read the wrong provider-account snapshot, and callers cannot implement a stable lookup contract.
items.impact: Cross-actor credential/account state collision, disclosure, replay corruption, and non-deterministic audit records.
items.builder_discretion: Specify a canonical composite identity, scope boundaries, uniqueness and migration rules, then define atomic read/write semantics.

evidence.exact_quote: - storage-plan does not key provider account snapshots only by run_id when runtime actors include non-run actors.

items.title: Support drift has no authority or reconciliation protocol
items.statement: The requirement forbids disagreement but does not name the authoritative file, update ordering, atomicity boundary, conflict detector, repair owner, rollback, or behavior when one file is missing or malformed. Parallel writers and interrupted updates can leave an undecidable state.
items.impact: Governance generation can oscillate, consume stale values, or silently reconcile in different directions.
items.builder_discretion: Define one authority and a transactional compare-and-repair protocol with explicit failure outcomes.

evidence.exact_quote: - sharding_config and auto_decisions do not disagree on fallback chunk-line settings.

items.title: Canonical label policy omits versioned aliases and translated accessibility copy
items.statement: Preventing alternate peer terms does not define whether machine tokens, visible English labels, accessible names, localized strings, historical persisted labels, and API aliases share one namespace. Literal enforcement can either break localization and migration or permit semantic drift through ungoverned aliases.
items.impact: Screen readers, translated UI, stored records, integrations, and older clients can disagree on state meaning.
items.builder_discretion: Separate stable semantic identifiers from locale-specific visible and accessible copy, with a versioned alias migration table.

evidence.exact_quote: - /labels, /action, /runtime, and /object consumers do not invent alternate peer terms.

items.title: Discovered-work routing lacks decision authority and transition guards
items.statement: The binary destination is named, but the deciding actor, admissibility criteria, idempotency key, graph-cycle and fan-out limits, concurrent duplicate discovery behavior, rejection path, and rollback after an invalid graph patch are absent.
items.impact: Equivalent discoveries can create duplicate remediation nodes or conflicting graph patches and destabilize the canonical graph.
items.builder_discretion: Define an authorized, idempotent discovery-classification transition with bounded graph mutation and compensating action.

evidence.exact_quote: - Newly discovered work becomes remediation nodes or graph-patch requests.

items.title: Integration quality has no falsifiable completion oracle
items.statement: Requiring integration quality is directionally correct but gives no required evidence, threshold, evaluator, freshness bound, conflict rule, or negative test that distinguishes a genuinely complete seam from locally passing packages.
items.impact: Different implementations can promote the same seam inconsistently while all claiming conformance.
items.builder_discretion: Specify observable integration evidence and deterministic promotion/rejection criteria.

evidence.exact_quote: - "Seam completion requires integration quality rather than package-local pass states alone."

items.title: Seams UI can present stale or partial summaries as current truth
items.statement: Visible summarization is required without loading, unavailable, partial, stale, recomputing, permission-denied, or data-source mismatch states. Network loss or partial backend failure can therefore leave a plausible summary that appears authoritative.
items.impact: Operators may promote or investigate based on incomplete or obsolete weak-integration evidence.
items.builder_discretion: Define provenance, freshness, completeness, error and retry states that cannot be confused with an empty clean summary.

evidence.exact_quote: - Seams UI visibly summarizes weak integration.

items.title: Weak-integration buckets lack scale, localization, and accessibility behavior
items.statement: Named headings do not define ordering, overflow, pagination or virtualization, duplicate aggregation, empty buckets, long translated headings, keyboard navigation, screen-reader grouping, color-independent severity, or small-screen behavior.
items.impact: Large or translated seams can become unreadable or inaccessible while still satisfying the heading-name check.
items.builder_discretion: Add bounded rendering and accessible semantic-group behavior independent of English label length and visual color.

evidence.exact_quote: - Weak integration concerns are grouped under readable headings including Wiring, Workflow, State, GUI, and Design.

items.title: Revoked and reopened names are not a transition system
items.statement: The list of explicit states lacks allowed from/to edges, precedence when patch and new evidence race, authorization, compare-and-set generation, idempotency, supersession behavior, terminality, retry, and recovery after a partially applied revocation.
items.impact: A seam can simultaneously appear complete, revoked, and reopened across consumers, or lose the event that should invalidate promotion.
items.builder_discretion: Define a versioned state machine with authorized commands, deterministic race resolution, event identity, and reconciliation.

evidence.exact_quote: - Promotion Revoked, Seam Completion Revoked, Reopened, Reopened by Patch, and Reopened by New Evidence remain explicit named states.

items.title: Blocked context has no privacy, lifecycle, or trust boundary
items.statement: Exposing reason, owner, and recovery context does not define who may write or read those fields, escaping and sanitization, sensitive-data prohibition, redaction, retention, owner identity lifecycle, or what the UI shows when access is denied.
items.impact: Untrusted or sensitive diagnostic content can leak through UI and logs, misattribute ownership, or become a persistent injection surface.
items.builder_discretion: Define structured allowlisted fields, authorization, redaction and retention, plus safe unavailable-state rendering.

evidence.exact_quote: - Blocked states expose blocked reason, blocked owner, and recovery context.

items.title: Approval anchors do not prevent stale replay or cross-scope authorization
items.statement: The identity fields do not define a unique namespace, actor and permission binding, nonce or expiry, expected blocked-sequence compare, duplicate command semantics, or behavior when the episode advances while an offline approval is submitted.
items.impact: A valid approval can be replayed against the wrong node, newer blocked episode, run, tenant, or execution unit and trigger unintended progression.
items.builder_discretion: Bind approvals to an authorized principal and immutable episode version with expiry and atomic stale-command rejection.

evidence.exact_quote: Approval anchoring moves to canonical runtime identity: run_id, node_id,

items.title: Optional attempt identity creates ambiguous approval migration
items.statement: Making attempt_id optional gives no discriminator for when absence is legal, how multi-attempt nodes avoid aliasing, whether old records are upgraded, or how mixed-version clients compare anchors.
items.impact: Approvals for different attempts can collapse onto one episode or become unreadable after schema migration.
items.builder_discretion: Define versioned identity forms, mandatory conditions, canonical normalization and backward-read rules.

evidence.exact_quote: blocked_sequence, optional attempt_id, and execution-unit context refs

items.title: Validation surfaces do not prove runtime semantics
items.statement: The repeated migration and index validators can establish structural plan consistency but no cited oracle exercises provider snapshot isolation, decision-file conflict recovery, label consumer conformance, graph transitions, stale UI states, reopen races, or approval replay.
items.impact: Every unit can pass its declared validation surfaces while its core negative-space failures remain executable.
items.builder_discretion: Add feature-specific executable contract, race, fault-injection, migration, UI-state and authorization tests.

items.title: Approval side effects have no destructive-action guard or compensation
items.statement: Changing CTA framing and identity does not specify confirmation for high-impact approvals, a dry-run preview, post-approval cancellation window, revocation authority, or compensation if downstream promotion partially executes.
items.impact: An accurately anchored but mistaken approval can irreversibly advance or mutate a graph without a defined recovery path.
items.builder_discretion: Classify approval consequences and require confirmation, idempotent execution and compensating transitions where effects are reversible.

evidence.exact_quote: - Request-centric button copy, persistence language, and tier-boundary CTA framing are superseded.

items.title: Cross-document ownership lists do not define propagation
items.statement: Implementation surfaces and owner hints enumerate documents but do not assign the canonical field owner, consumer obligations, schema-version handshake, update order, incompatibility behavior, or enforcement at each seam.
items.impact: Decision_Log can be internally coherent while storage, models, UI, policy, contracts and progression gates interpret the same decision differently.
items.builder_discretion: For each feature, designate one contract owner and enumerate versioned producer/consumer assertions and failure behavior.

items.title: Complete caller and consumer population is not knowable from the window
items.statement: The listed implementation surfaces may not exhaust persisted records, APIs, automation, exports, notifications, plugins, telemetry, or older clients that consume these identities, labels, states and approvals; the window supplies no closed-world consumer registry.
items.impact: Unlisted consumers can preserve deprecated identity or state semantics and defeat otherwise correct migrations.
items.builder_discretion: Require a machine-checkable producer/consumer registry before declaring cross-document migration complete.

items.title: Provider runtime scope explicitly extends beyond Orchestrator
items.statement: The unit explicitly identifies assistant and other non-Orchestrator provider-runtime actors, so omission of non-run actor categories at the high-level scope is not a gap.

evidence.exact_quote: The shared provider-runtime contract applies beyond Orchestrator to assistant,

items.title: Weak integration is required to be visibly summarized
items.statement: The UI requirement rejects badge-only treatment and requires a visible seam summary, so basic weak-integration discoverability is explicitly addressed.

evidence.exact_quote: Seams UI must summarize weak integration visibly, group concerns under

items.title: Blocked states have minimum diagnostic context
items.statement: The requirement explicitly names reason, owner and recovery context as visible blocked-state data; their existence is addressed even though access, privacy and lifecycle rules are not.

evidence.exact_quote: expose blocked reason, blocked owner, and recovery context, weak-integration

items.title: Gate and evidence schema mismatch is explicitly a defect
items.statement: The unit makes schema mismatch a first-class governance defect rather than permitting a silent evidence interpretation mismatch.

evidence.exact_quote: first-class governance defect that evidence contracts must expose.

dimension_assessments.summary: Provider identity and cross-document consumer populations are not closed or contractually assigned.
Discovered-work, reopen/revocation and optional-attempt states lack complete transition invariants.
Snapshot writes, support-file updates, reopen commands and approvals have no deterministic concurrency contract.
Interrupted governance updates, partial UI data, graph mutation and approval execution lack defined outcomes.
Reconciliation, graph-patch rollback, state repair and approval compensation are unspecified.
Writers, adjudicators, transition actors, context viewers and approval principals are not normatively bound.
Provider snapshots and blocked diagnostic context lack scope, retention, redaction and deletion semantics.
Support records, blocked context and approval identities lack validation, escaping and stale-input rejection contracts.
Visible weak-integration truth has no stale, partial, unavailable or permission-limited states despite good baseline visibility.
Offline UI data and delayed approvals have no freshness or stale-command behavior.
Graph-patch growth and large concern collections have no bounds or rendering strategy.
Canonical labels and grouped concern views omit accessible-name, navigation and nonvisual semantics.
Literal canonical labels and English headings are not separated from localized presentation.
Snapshot identity, label aliases and optional attempt identity lack mixed-version migration rules.
Freshness, redaction and semantic executable receipts are absent from support behavior.
Approval-triggered progression has no impact classification, confirmation or compensation contract.
Document lists do not define owner/consumer propagation or version handshakes.
Integration quality is subjective and generic validators do not execute the specified behaviors or failures.
No closed-world registry establishes that all external and legacy consumers are represented in this window.
